newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan January trade data - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan January trade data - Reuters poll.

text.p: The following Reuters poll of economists gives projections for Taiwan's imports and exports in January and year-on-year growth.
Official figures were to be issued by the Finance Ministry at 0245 on Wednesday, two days ahead of schedule due to the lunar new year holiday, which falls this year on February 7.
Note: Figures are in billion of U.S. dollars. Change is year-on-year percentage change. Brackets ( ) indicate negative growth.
Institution Exports chg Imports chg Balance chg

The poll results produced an average forecast for January exports of US$10.308 billion, which would represent a 3.57 percent decline from January 1996, and January imports of US$9.486 billion, down 1.69 percent from January 1996.
They produced an average forecast for a January trade surplus of US$822 million, down 21.11 percent from a year ago.

December 1996 showed a trade surplus of US$2.183 billion, up 69.2 percent from December 1995, which brought the full-year 1996 trade surplus to US$14.704 billion, itself a 81.3 percent year-on-year rise.
In January 1996, exports were US$10.69 billion and imports were US$9.649 billion, giving a rounded trade surplus of US$1.042 billion.
Economists attributed the forecasts of negative January growth to the unusually high comparative base in January 1996.
"Both exports and imports were in a peak in January 1996," said HSBC James Capel economist Steven Wang.

Capital Securities economist Wang Chia-yuan suggested that January and February trade performance should be taken together to best discern an accurate trend, saying the variable date of the lunar new year always skewed one or the other.
"Each year, the Chinese new year holidays fall in either January or February, and exporters do not accord in delivering products before or after the holidays," Wang said.

The new year holiday usually lasts for some five days, but manufacturers always take a longer rest, a factor that accentuates the holiday's impact on the export value in the month in which it falls, economists said.
